content.text:
Item #2348 ran and converged `done`.

**What the run did** — converted two `headless-browser` prose rules into three declared checks, retiring both bullets whole:

| Prose retired | Became |
|---|---|
| *Wait on something the page itself produces, never on the network going quiet.* | `headless-browser/networkidle-wait` (block) + `headless-browser/capture-without-font-wait` (advise) |
| *Use an `https` fake origin.* | `headless-browser/insecure-fake-origin` (block) |

The wait bullet carried two rules in one breath, so clearing it took two checks — they split rather than share a declaration because the font half's relevance gate is narrower (tracked reference images) and a declaration's gate is whole-spec.

**Proof.** 22 fixtures across three suites. Every branch of every check — the match, each exemption, the relevance gate, the scan scope, the comment stripping — was mutated away in turn and the fixture guarding it watched to go red, then restored. Full suite green (4050), `check_the_world` 0 blocking, `check_the_work` 0 blocking (the two `rules-append-only` advisories are the deliberate retirements, said in the PR as that check's fix line asks).

**Folders touched**

| Folder | What changed |
|---|---|
| `packs/headless-browser/` | new `declared-checks.json` with the three checks; two bullets deleted from `RULES.md`; README gains a Checks table and drops the two rule rows; three fixture suites under `test/` |
| `packs/headless-browser/provenance/` | `retired` entries on the two rule files, `born` on the three check files, a `declined` entry recording the clip, launch-reuse, animation-freeze and binary-resolution rules and why they were left |
| `packs/` | the shelf catalog row for headless-browser: 0 checks → 3, 22 rules → 20 |

**Judgement calls worth a reviewer's eye.** `capture-without-font-wait` ships advisory rather than blocking: the "does anything here await fonts" probe is repo-wide, so the wait may legitimately sit in a shared helper, and that tolerance is what it trades its grade for. `insecure-fake-origin` spares loopback, which browsers already treat as a secure origin — a narrowing of the rule as written, and the correct one; it does *not* catch an origin reaching `goto` through a variable, and the allowlist form that would was rejected on its `packs/headless-browser/provenance/headless-browser-insecure-fake-origin.md` entry, because a parameterised `goto` is ordinary in a capture harness.

[PR #2364](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2364) merged squash under the task's `under:packs` policy (`AUTOMERGE: yes`; auto-merge refused as "clean status", so merged directly per the delivery procedure). [Item #2348](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2348) closed `task:status:done`. No production verification filed — the fixtures that ran are the mechanism. Session captured under the item.

> ✅ All done

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/writing-repo-scanning-checks

# Writing a check that scans the repo

- **Choosing the file set** — take it from `git ls-files` rather than a filesystem walk with
  paths to skip, and remember a brand-new file is untracked until you add it, so a green run
  isn't coverage of it. (choosing-file-set)

- **Scanning for a forbidden token** — strip comments first so it matches code, not prose —
  string-aware, since a `//` inside a URL is not a comment. Reuse `stripComments` from
  [`engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs`](../../../../engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs);
  if the scan can't import it, inline the same pass and point a comment back at that source.
  Strip in **both** directions — a comment that documents or warns about the banned pattern is
  exactly where a naive check trips over its own reasoning, so a commented-out instance must not
  count as present either. (scanning-forbidden-token)

- **Proving the check silent** — run it against the repo's own **real** sources, not only a
  synthetic clean fixture — a fixture spelling the same gap the check has just keeps proving the
  matching, and only a real-tree run can disagree with you. (proving-check-silent)

input.title: Keep the headless-browser checks off their own fixture files
input.head: claudinite/canon-prose-to-checks-self-exclude
input.body:
A follow-up to #2364, found by the step that skill asks for and that run did not reach until after the merge: running the three new checks over this repo's **real** tree rather than only synthetic fixtures.

Two of them were not silent. `headless-browser/networkidle-wait` reported nine findings and `headless-browser/insecure-fake-origin` five — every one of them inside the fixture file that exists to spell the shape the check bans.

The engine gives a **skill-scoped** `declared-checks.json` a `selfExclude` for its own directory (`loadDeclaredChecks`) and gives a **pack-root** one nothing, so each of the three checks now names the pack path in its `excludeFiles` alternation. A clean fixture per check pins it, and each was proved to go red with the exclusion removed.

Nothing changes for a member repo: its copy of the pack lives under `.claudinite/shared/`, which `ctx.files` never scans. The exclusion only ever matters in the canon, which is also the only place the fixtures exist.

Verified: the real-tree probe now reports 0 findings for all three; 25 fixtures green; full suite 4056 passing; `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` both 0 blocking.

Refs #2348

input.commit_title: Keep the headless-browser checks off their own fixture files (#2368)
input.commit_message:
A real-tree run of the three checks landed in #2364 found two of them firing
nine and five times on the fixtures that exist to spell the shapes they ban.
The engine self-excludes a skill-scoped declaration's own directory and a
pack-root one's not at all, so each check's excludeFiles now names the pack
path, with a clean fixture per check proved to bite when it is removed.

No member sees the difference: its copy of the pack sits under the mount,
which is never scanned.

Refs #2348
